public_rationale: OpenAI's July 22, 2025 announcement confirms an agreement with Oracle for 4.5GW of additional Stargate capacity, but does not establish exclusive customer dependence or complete repayment arrangements [e2]. Oracle's filing for February 28, 2026 describes senior notes issued for general corporate purposes, without allocating proceeds or repayment sources to individual Stargate projects [e1]. These disclosures do not establish exclusive reliance on OpenAI and project cash receipts, or a viable replacement customer for the revenue at issue [e1, e2].
limitations: Complete project contracts, guarantees and repayment models are absent.
Corporate debt terms do not quantify project-specific funding or expected repayment support.
The evidence does not test replacement-customer feasibility during December 2025–February 2026.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Oracle has no other path to making this revenue without OpenAI, and these projects are entirely financed and paid for using the projected cashflow of the data centers themselves.

statement.excerpt: I really need to be clear that Oracle has no other path to making this revenue without OpenAI, and these projects are entirely financed and paid for using the projected cashflow of the data centers themselves.

from_speaker: Oracle has no other path to making this revenue without OpenAI
using the projected cashflow of the data centers themselves
our_interpretation: This revenue means the projected revenue from the Stargate projects discussed immediately beforehand, not all Oracle revenue.
The ordinary reading is that the projects depend exclusively on OpenAI demand and their expected cash receipts to justify funding and repay their costs.
The words do not expressly say that every loan is legally non-recourse. Corporate borrowing alone therefore does not conclusively refute the economic-dependence claim.

Use the latest reported Oracle fiscal quarter before the post as the financing baseline. Earlier project agreements and later syndication reports are context unless they establish arrangements within that period.
criteria.support_condition: Project contracts and financing records establish exclusive dependence on OpenAI for the projected revenue and complete reliance on project cash receipts for funding recovery, with no commercially viable replacement demand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Project-specific records establish material independent revenue or repayment support, or a commercially viable alternative customer arrangement capable of replacing the revenue at issue.

evidence.explanation: Oracle's corporate debt has broader recourse than a loan secured solely on a project. This cautions against reading the claim as a universal description of legal recourse, but does not establish which funds support Stargate or what revenues are expected to repay them.
This confirms OpenAI's central role in the announced capacity agreement. It neither proves the absence of alternative customers nor discloses all financing and repayment sources.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Project contracts and financing models applicable to December 2025–February 2026 showing customer exclusivity, funding sources, guarantees and repayment support, together with evidence testing commercially viable replacement demand for the same capacity and revenue.
